facts: In late April 2023, 20 to 70 cm of snow fell in Dalarna, Värmland, Västernorrland, and Jämtland, causing many golden eagle nests to fail.
In 2023, Sweden recorded 498.5 occupied golden eagle territories, but only 166 nests produced chicks — the lowest success rate since 2018.
Gotland recorded the highest number of occupied golden eagle territories since monitoring began, showing a positive trend for the species on the island.
Golden eagles avoid human activity and need undisturbed nesting sites. Nesting failure can occur due to disturbance, lack of suitable trees, and reduced prey like grouse and hares.

Protecting golden eagles involves identifying and preserving nesting sites. Over 80% of nests are on state land, with about 40% in conservation areas. Forestry near nests is banned during the breeding season to prevent disturbance.
In 2023, geese caused about SEK 130 million in agricultural damage, a 50% increase from 2020. Meanwhile, interest in goose hunting is declining, creating an imbalance.
Interest in goose hunting has cooled, likely because greylag and barnacle geese are harder to hunt than the now rarer Canada geese, especially in Skåne.
Goose populations have increased sharply in Sweden in recent decades, causing issues for both farmers and bathers. Research is underway to understand the causes and find solutions.
A study of 176 captured and X-rayed greylag geese found that one in five had between 1 and 16 shotgun pellets embedded in their bodies — a concerning sign.
A new survey method introduced in 2013 may explain the recorded decline in wolverine numbers, but further research is needed to confirm if it's a real decrease or a data issue.
Up to 90% of wolverine deaths in Sweden are due to illegal hunting.
According to Svensk Jakt, wolverine hunting in border areas far exceeds the annual growth target.

From 1995 to 2005, 49 cases of suspected illegal wolverine hunting were reported, but only six were investigated. Researchers estimate around 50 wolverines are poached each year, suggesting most cases go undetected.
The breeding success of female wolverines varies each year, with some years seeing more successful litters than others.
